Stantonbury School is a vibrant school striving for every student to achieve their full potential in a happy and secure environment.

Welcome from the Principal
It is a real pleasure to welcome you to Stantonbury School. I speak to you with both honesty and optimism for our future: while we recognise that the school has experienced a period of change and challenge, we are now firmly in an ambitious journey of transformation. Supported by the Tove Learning Trust, we are moving forward with renewed energy, clear direction, and an unwavering commitment to ensuring that every young person at Stantonbury School recognises their potential and is empowered to achieve it. I feel incredibly privileged to lead this new chapter as we build a culture in which our students can truly thrive.
My mission as Principal is rooted in a strong moral purpose: I believe that every child, without exception, deserves the opportunity to succeed. True success, however, is about far more than academic achievement alone. It is equally important that our students feel safe, supported, and confident in their learning environment. At Stantonbury School, we are creating a culture built on kindness, integrity, aspiration, and respect, where every student feels valued as an individual and encouraged to become the very best version of themselves.
To achieve this, we operate under a “Professional Parent” model. This means our staff are committed to supporting every student with the same care, high expectations, and encouragement that any parent would want for their child. We provide guidance, consistency, and “firm but fair” boundaries that help young people develop confidence, resilience, and strong character. We want Stantonbury School to be a school where families feel reassured, students feel inspired, and education extends far beyond the classroom itself.
We are determined to create an environment where intellectual curiosity is celebrated and where students develop a genuine love of learning. Through high-quality teaching, enriching experiences, and a broad curriculum, we encourage our young people to think deeply, ask questions, and engage with the world around them. Alongside academic success, we place great importance on personal growth, recognising that education should prepare students not only for examinations, but for life.
Our vision is to develop well-rounded individuals through a rich programme of extracurricular opportunities and meaningful experiences that allow students to flourish both academically and personally. Whether through our “Career Kickstarter” courses, our partnership with the MK Dons Community Trust, or international cultural visits to Paris and Ypres, we prepare our students for the opportunities and responsibilities of adult life. We encourage our students to think ambitiously about their futures and to understand that, through hard work and determination, exceptional outcomes are achievable.
At the same time, we want our students to recognise the importance of compassion, service, and contributing positively to their community. We believe that success should be accompanied by humility, empathy, and a desire to make a difference in the lives of others. Our aim is for every student to leave Stantonbury School not only with strong qualifications, but also with the confidence, integrity, and sense of purpose needed to become thoughtful, responsible, and successful adults.
By working closely with our families through our Professional Parent approach, we build the strong partnerships needed to guide and support our young people throughout their educational journey. Together, we are shaping a bright and ambitious future in which every student at Stantonbury School is empowered to succeed, contribute positively to society, and realise the full extent of their potential.
Mrs Natasha Bryan, Principal

pageCache.text:
Student Absence: absence@stantonbury.tove.org.uk
Year 10 Students Inspired by 'Careers at the YMCA' Experience
A group of our Year 10 students took part in an inspiring and educational ‘Careers at the YMCA’ event in central Milton Keynes.
The visit to the YMCA Headquarters marked the successful conclusion of a series of in-school workshops designed to develop key employability skills and prepare our young people for the future.
Exploring Diverse Career Pathways
During their time at the HQ, students had the unique opportunity to meet with several members of the YMCA team. Staff members provided invaluable first-hand insight into their daily job roles, responsibilities, and the diverse career pathways available within the organisation.
The visit concluded with a series of tailored 1:1 meetings with the YMCA’s professional career advisor. These sessions focused on practical steps for entering the workforce, including:
Outstanding Representation from Stantonbury Students
Our students thoroughly enjoyed the experience, describing the sessions as inspiring, useful, and a fascinating eye-opener to rewarding careers they never knew existed.
We are also incredibly proud to report that the YMCA staff commented very favourably on our pupils. They highly praised the hard work, positive attitude, and exemplary conduct demonstrated by the group throughout the visit. They were fantastic ambassadors for Stantonbury School.
With Special Thanks
An initiative like this relies on strong community partnerships. The Careers Team would like to extend a huge thank you to the staff at the YMCA for hosting such an impactful day.
We would also like to express our gratitude to our friends at Ethos for their invaluable support in helping to house and facilitate the preparatory workshops leading up to this trip.
Presented by the Stantonbury School Careers Team

pageCache.pageTitle: Stantonbury School - A Night to Remember at Stadium MK: Year 10 Footballers Shine in TOVE 10 Charity Match
pageCache.text:
Student Absence: absence@stantonbury.tove.org.uk
A Night to Remember at Stadium MK: Year 10 Footballers Shine in TOVE 10 Charity Match
Our Year 10 boys’ football team recently traded the school fields for the big leagues, stepping out onto the professional pitch at Stadium MK for the highly anticipated Stantonbury TOVE 10 Charity Match.
Facing off against our fellow Tove Learning Trust rivals, Lord Grey Academy, this was more than just a game. For most of these lads, walking through the tunnel and playing in a professional stadium is a lifelong dream—and they gave it absolutely everything they had from the first whistle to the last.
Incredible Support in the Stands
We didn’t just bring a team to Stadium MK; we brought the entire Stantonbury community! Around 100 fantastic Year 10 students packed into the stands to cheer on their classmates, creating an electric atmosphere from start to finish.
The creativity on display was brilliant, with students bringing along handmade posters dedicated to our star players. More importantly, the conduct of every single student in attendance was an absolute credit to Stantonbury School. They represented us with pride, passion, and impeccable behavior, proving that our off-pitch support is just as world-class as our on-pitch effort.
A Hard-Fought Battle and the Real Win
The match itself was a nail-biter. After a grueling, hard-fought battle on the pitch, the final whistle blew with a narrow 3-2 loss for Stantonbury. While the scoreboard wasn't quite in our favour, the real victory happened off the pitch.
Thanks to the incredible generosity of everyone who bought tickets and supported the event, we raised £200 for Willen Hospice!
"Win or lose, memories were made, funds were raised for an incredible cause, and our students showed what Stantonbury is truly all about."
Thank You!
A massive thank you goes out to Lord Grey Academy for a fantastic, competitive game, and to MK Dons for being such incredible hosts. Finally, a huge thank you to all the parents, staff, and students who came out to make it a night we won't soon forget.
#TOVE10 #StantonburyPride #Community

pageCache.pageTitle: Stantonbury School - Year 7 French Adventure: Stantonbury Students Explore the Historic Streets of Lille
pageCache.text:
Student Absence: absence@stantonbury.tove.org.uk
Year 7 French Adventure: Stantonbury Students Explore the Historic Streets of Lille
A whistle-stop day trip filled with cultural immersion, sweet treats, and outstanding representation of our school values.
Our wonderful Year 7 students embarked on an unforgettable cross-channel day trip to the beautiful city of Lille, France. It was an action-packed, fast-paced journey, and our students proved themselves to be exceptional ambassadors for Stantonbury School every step of the way!
Soaking in French Culture and History
The adventure began with a sensory journey through the Halles de Wazemmes, a bustling traditional covered market, where students experienced the vibrant sights, sounds, and smells of local French commerce.
From there, the group traveled deeper into the heart of the city, standing in awe of the stunning architecture at the historic Grand Place and the grand facade of the Palais des Beaux-Arts.
Of course, no trip to France is complete without sampling the local delicacies! There were smiles all around as the students treated themselves to world-famous chocolates from Le Lautrec and enjoyed delicious, historic treats from the famous Méert ice cream stand.
Living Our Values Abroad
Throughout this rapid-fire excursion, our Year 7s didn’t just observe French culture—they actively lived out the core values of Stantonbury School:
A True Test of Endurance!
An excursion of this scale is no small feat. The journey began with a bright and early departure at 3:00 AM and concluded with a tired but happy arrival back at school at 1:00 AM the following morning. Taking a 22-hour travel day in their stride is a massive achievement for our Year 7s.
"A massive thank you to all of the dedicated staff members who gave up their time to make this brilliant trip possible, and a huge well done to Year 7. You were fantastic ambassadors for Stantonbury School!"

Year 9 Options
Your Future, Your Choice: Year 9 Options 2026
This is an important term for our Year 9 students as they begin the exciting journey of selecting their Key Stage 4 Option Choices.
We have designed a comprehensive support programme to help you and your child make realistic, relevant, and ambitious choices for their future.
Step 1: Review Progress
Before making any decisions, we recommend logging into My Child At School (MCAS) to review your child’s Autumn Term report. This is the perfect starting point to discuss their current strengths and areas for development.
Step 2: Year 9 Parents’ Evening
Date: Thursday 26th February
Location: On-site (Face-to-face appointments)
Join us to discuss academic progress and potential Key Stage 4 pathways with subject teachers.
How to Book: The booking system opens Wednesday 4th February at midday and closes Thursday 26th February at 13:00.
If you cannot attend, please contact teachers directly via email: This email address is being protected from spambots. You need JavaScript enabled to view it..
Log into School Cloud.
Click on 'Parents' Evening Booking System'.
Check your email for confirmation.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stantonbury School - Introducing The Stantonbury Way: Our New Vision and Core Values
pageCache.text:
Student Absence: absence@stantonbury.tove.org.uk
Introducing The Stantonbury Way: Our New Vision and Core Values
We are thrilled to officially announce the launch of The Stantonbury Way. A foundational milestone that defines who we are, what we stand for, and how we guide our students toward a bright and successful future.
At the heart of this initiative is a clear and powerful mission. Our ultimate goal is to empower all students to achieve excellence, act with integrity, show kindness, nurture curiosity, and aspire to make a positive impact in the world around them. To bring this vision to life and embed it into our daily school culture, we have established five core values. Going forward, these pillars will guide our students and staff in everything they do:
Genuine Kindness
Authentic Integrity
Intellectual Curiosity
Noble Aspirations
Determined Excellence
Living Our Values Every Day
These five values are more than just words on a page; they represent the standards we hold ourselves both at Stantonbury School and beyond our school gates.
By focusing on these principles, we ensure that a Stantonbury education shapes not just academic success, but strong character.
We look forward to working closely with our students, families, and staff to bring The Stantonbury Way to life every single day. Thank you for your continued support as we embark on this exciting new chapter together.

Student Leadership
Through various leadership roles, students are encouraged to take ownership of their school community and contribute to decision-making processes happening at our school. These roles can include Year Reps or Vice Reps and being a member of all the different councils or committees going on around the school, all of whom work together to ensure that student voices are heardand that the school environment is inclusive and supportive.
The student leadership program at Stantonbury aims to empower students by giving them the opportunity to lead projects, organise events, and provide guidance to their peers. Leaders are encouraged to act as role models, demonstrating qualities such as respect, integrity, and teamwork.
Through these experiences, students develop crucial life skills, including communication, problem-solving, and time management, which are valuable both in their academic journey and future endeavours.
Moreover, Stantonbury Secondary School’s approach to student leadership fosters a strong sense of community and belonging. The school recognises that students, by working together and assuming leadership roles, can drive change and create a positive school culture. This collaborative approach not only enhances the student experience but also instill a sense of pride and ownership in the school's achievements, helping to create a vibrant and engaged student body.

pageCache.text:
Student Absence: absence@stantonbury.tove.org.uk
Navigating the Future: Year 9 Explore the Journey to Adulthood
At Stantonbury School, our Religious Education (RE) curriculum is designed to do more than just teach world religions, it aims to equip students with the perspective and practical skills they need to navigate modern life. Recently, our Year 9 students have been immersed in a vital unit of study: The Transition into Adulthood.
More Than Just a Milestone
Transitioning into adulthood is a pivotal moment in any young person's life. To support our students during this time, the Year 9 curriculum has expanded to include essential life skills that bridge the gap between the classroom and the real world.
Students have been actively engaging with:
A Global Perspective on Maturity
A key element of this topic is understanding how different communities celebrate and manage the move into adulthood. Students have examined how the six major world religions prepare their youth for the responsibilities of adult life, looking at how faith influences lifestyle choices and ethical decisions.
To ensure a comprehensive understanding of society today, the classes also explored Humanist and Atheist perspectives. By comparing these diverse worldviews, students gain a deeper appreciation for the variety of beliefs they will encounter in their future careers and communities.
Why This Matters in Year 9
Year 9 is a significant year of transition. As students begin to make choices about their GCSE options and start defining their own personal identities, this unit encourages critical thinking and independence. "By exploring these diverse perspectives and practical skills, we are helping our students prepare for the real-life responsibilities they will face as they move towards adulthood."
We are incredibly impressed with the maturity our Year 9s have shown in discussing these complex topics, showing great respect for the diverse lifestyles and beliefs that make up our modern world.

pageCache.text:
Student Absence: absence@stantonbury.tove.org.uk
Stantonbury Sixth Form Students Celebrate Success and Ambitious Futures
Students at Stantonbury Sixth Form are celebrating another year of success as they secure places at leading universities, progress into higher level apprenticeships and take exciting next steps towards their future careers.
This year's results reflect the determination and ambition of young adults who have embraced opportunities both inside and outside the classroom. Students will now progress to a wide range of destinations including, but never limited to, prestigious places at Russell Group universities, professional apprenticeships, employment, exciting gap years and specialist training programmes- including our very own firefighter of the future!
Leading the way is Ezra, who achieved an exceptional set of results with A* grades in Chemistry, Mathematics and Music, alongside an A grade in Mandarin. Ezra will now embark on missionary service in California, continuing a journey that reflects both academic excellence and a commitment to serving others.
Another outstanding success story is Mohamed who achieved A* in Mathematics and A grades in Physics, Chemistry and Further Mathematics. Moha has secured a place to study Mechanical Engineering at the University of Bristol, one of the UK's leading universities.
Rowan achieved an impressive A grade in Physics, A grade in Chemistry and A grade in Mathematics and will progress to the University of Birmingham to study Mechanical Engineering.
Other notable achievements include Alfie, who achieved A, A, B in History, English Literature and Psychology before securing a place at the University of Warwick to study History and Politics, and Anastasia, whose outstanding A* in Sociology has helped her progress to study Medicine at Anglia Ruskin University.
Students from Stantonbury Sixth Form have secured places at a range of highly regarded universities across the country, including the University of Bristol, University of Birmingham, University of Warwick, University of Nottingham, Newcastle University and the University of York. Courses being studied include Medicine, Mechanical Engineering, Economics, Biomedical Science, History and Politics, Law, Psychology and Accounting and Finance.
The Sixth Form is equally proud of students pursuing apprenticeship and employment pathways. This year, students have secured apprenticeships with national organisations including Network Rail and Bellway Homes, while others have progressed into employment, military service, the excitement of gap years, specialist training and international volunteering opportunities. This is so reflective of the young people that we serve and their ambition for both future success and a belief that we hold firmly - determined excellence.
Principal's Statement
"We continue to be incredibly proud of everything our students have achieved. These results are a reflection of their dedication, focus and hard work, supported by our committed staff and wider school community. Whether progressing to university, apprenticeships, employment or other incredible and exciting opportunities, every student should be proud of their achievements. We look forward to seeing what they accomplish in the future and wish them every success in the next stage of their journey. We ask them to keep in touch, as we are always genuinely curious and excited about the paths our students lives take beyond school "
Everyone at Stantonbury Sixth Form extends its warmest congratulations to the Class of 2026 and wishes them every success as they begin the next chapter of their lives.

Careers
Stantonbury School has developed a careers programme that meets the requirements of the government’s Provider Access Legislation and the Gatsby Benchmarks of good careers guidance.
Our aim is to develop student employability skills, resilience and career management skills and inform students about local, national and international labour markets. Students are guided to explore and develop career ideas and high aspirations; they are educated on the complete spectrum of post-16 and post-18 transitions.
Information for Stantonbury School Families
Families are encouraged to support their children by discussing careers based activities, and opportunities with them, Please use the following weblink to get you started:https://cdn.unifrog.org/downloads/Parent_caregiver_conversation_starters.pdf.
It is also important to ensure that your child is aware of their wonderful positive personality traits and skills, as they will need to have a great understanding of themselves to be able to make successful transition plans. A good way of encouraging your child to become more self-aware is to support them to complete the personality profile, the interest profile, the skills profile and the work environment profile on Unifrog.
Link: https://www.unifrog.org/.
Our Careers team is happy to work in partnership with families to support students and this includes hosting family meetings to discuss and explore job roles, study and training pathways.
Our Careers team attend key school events, such as Year 9 options evenings and Sixth Form Open Evening and are happy to meet with students and their families.
Information for Teachers and Other Staff
Staff play a central role in the careers education and learning that our students experience. Staff contribute effectively through:
Unifrog: students and staff have their own log in for the Unifrog platform, which enables students to create their own careers learning and preparation journey. Tutors and subject staff can utilise its teaching resources to support students with refining their interests, learning about different industries and job sectors as well as giving feedback on students’ CVs and personal statements. Link: https://www.unifrog.org/.
Staff can make referrals for personal guidance appointments and requests for support with arranging employer, further education or higher education events, trips or visits by emailing: This email address is being protected from spambots. You need JavaScript enabled to view it..
We aim to stay in touch with students after they have completed their education with us and welcome the input of our Alumni into our careers programme. This can also be done by UniFrog or by emailing: This email address is being protected from spambots. You need JavaScript enabled to view it..

Student Absence: absence@stantonbury.tove.org.uk
Careers Post-16 and Post-18 Pathways
Post-16 and Post-18 Pathways
Beginning to explore what you are going to do when you reach a transition point can be such an exciting time. However, for some students the breadth of choice can make the process feel overwhelming. Our careers team is available to support students to explore and make appropriate transition choices. Students from all year groups have access to our Head of Careers or Careers Adviser via the School’s lunchtime career drop-ins which run, Monday to Thursday, term-time (Friday for students who access our SEND base).
Year 11 students and their families are sent, up to date information on transition options for a range of academic abilities during the autumn term (this includes foundation learning for students who may need more one-to-one support). Year 11 students also receive an assembly detailing these options and are given information on the deadlines for making applications. Year 11 students receive personal guidance based on their job role preferences and academic ability. Where students are unsure of job role preferences they are supported to complete personality profiles which show their job role matches. Students’ progression with their transition plans are monitored and students are supported until they receive offers appropriate to their academic abilities. Each academic year, wherever possible the School will hold a Year 11 and Sixth Form Careers Fair to enable students to explore a wide range of career and study options; enabling them to make informed transition choices.
Students transitioning after Year 13 have the following opportunities:
How to decide what to do:
What do you enjoy? What subjects do you do best in? Do you have a passion for learning? Do you have job ideas? How do you prefer to learn?
Answering these questions will help students to workout which is the right study and training pathway for them. Additionally students all have access to our online careers platform - Unifrog.
All students have access to this excellent online careers platform. Link: https://www.unifrog.org/
Unifrog is a universal destinations platform, a one-stop-shop for whole-careers guidance. Its aim is to level the playing field when it comes to students searching for the best opportunities and applying successfully for courses, apprenticeships and work.
Unifrog is used in school within careers and PSHE, teaching staff refer to Unifrog at the start of each new topic and have access to a wide range of subject and careers related resources.
It is a platform that allows students to explore their positive personality traits, skills and working environment preferences. It provides teaching resources, short course information and a wealth of information on colleges, sixth forms, and universities in the UK and internationally, and apprenticeships. It has a large library of careers profiles and helpful Know-how guides on a wide range of topics (from writing a CV through to making Oxbridge applications).
Our Head of Careers strongly recommends its use to students, families and staff. Parents can seek advice from our Head of Careers, or Careers Adviser.
Further Transition Information:
Students: when you leave Stantonbury School we ask students and families to email our Careers Administrator with where you are transitioning to (sixth form, college, training provider, university, employer etc.), please email: This email address is being protected from spambots. You need JavaScript enabled to view it..
We will keep in contact with your family, to keep up to date with what you go on to do in terms of education and work. We will also advise on school careers events in case you wish to volunteer. We are always here to help, even after you leave school. Just email our Head of Careers and arrange a career appointment.
Remember, you have to be in some form of recognised study and training until your 18th birthday; so whilst you may go into employment aged 16-years, it must involve an element of accredited study towards that role for at least one-day-per-week.
Local and Regional Colleges:
Higher education (University or College)
Apprenticeships (including higher and degree apprenticeships)

Values
Our Vision & Values: The Stantonbury Way
Welcome to the heart of our school community. The Stantonbury Way defines who we are, what we stand for, and how we guide our students toward a bright, purposeful future.
Our Vision
To empower all students to achieve excellence, act with integrity, show kindness, nurture curiosity, and aspire to make a positive impact in the world around them.
Our Core Values
To bring this vision to life and embed it into our daily school culture, we have established five core values. These pillars serve as our guiding compass, shaping the actions of our students and staff in everything they do:
Genuine Kindness
Authentic Integrity
Intellectual Curiosity
Noble Aspirations
Determined Excellence
Shaping Character and Community
These five values are more than just words on a page; they represent the standards we hold ourselves to both at Stantonbury School and beyond our school gates. By focusing daily on these principles, we ensure that a Stantonbury education shapes not just academic success, but a character that can change the world.
We look forward to working closely with our students, families, and staff to bring The Stantonbury Way to life every single day.

Safeguarding
The school is committed to the vital contribution all governors and staff can make to safeguarding children. We will strive to make sure that every student in the school feels secure, well cared for, and able to reach their full potential.
We will ensure all our own staff, other professionals, parents/carers and students work together to know about keeping children safe. They will understand the importance of following procedures and listening to each other, especially when there are concerns about safety.
The school will work hard to reduce all the kinds of harm that children can suffer, including abuse, bullying, discrimination and avoidable injuries. If you have any concerns at all about the safety or welfare of a child please do not hesitate to contact us.
If you have any questions, worries or concerns do not hesitate to contact one of the Safeguarding team.
Calling the school reception and saying you have a confidential matter for the safeguarding team, leaving your name, number and a time for a call back

Pupil Premium Funding
Pupil Premium
The pupil premium is additional funding for publicly funded schools in England to raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils of all abilities and to close the gaps between them and their peers.
Schools receive the funding for each pupil:
Adoption
a special guardianship order
Pupil Premium Reports

pdf Pupil Premium Strategy Statement 2024-2025
pdf Pupil Premium Strategy Statement 2022-2023

Year 7 Catch Up Premium
The literacy and numeracy catch-up premium gives state-funded schools additional funding to support year 7 pupils who did not achieve the expected standard in reading or maths at the end of key stage 2 (KS2).
pdf Year 7 Catch Up Premium Strategy 2019-20
pdf Year 7 Catch Up Premium Strategy 2017-18
pdf Year 7 Catch Up Premium Strategy 2018-19
Catch Up Premium (COVID-19)
The government funding to support children and young people to catch up on lost learning time due to school closures includes:
pdf Catch Up Premium Plan (COVID 19)
a schools programme for 5 to 16-year-olds
a 16 to 19 tuition fund
16 – 19 Tuition Funding
Stantonbury School COVID-19 16-19 Tuition Fund Statement:
The 16 to 19 tuition fund will be used to provide small group tuition for students aged 16 to 19 who have not yet achieved a grade 5 or above in English and/or maths. The provision will not be limited to tuition for English and maths, but will also be used to help progressing students on vocational courses where assessment may have been deferred because of lockdown. Students with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) – including those aged 19 to 24 who require additional tuition to help them catch up with their studies – will also be supported by this provision.
Tuition groups will comprise of no more than five students and the tuition sessions will be scheduled in addition to the planned programme of study hours already timetabled for the academic year 2020/21. Tuition and additional support may be delivered using a blend of online and on-campus delivery.Examples of some of the Tuition Support on offer will include:
Tuition Support offered will be based on an individual needs assessment, the identification of an individual starting point, clear learning goals, expectations and outcomes.
GCSE exam resit preparation
Functional skills assessment preparation
Vocational deferred assessment preparation
Vocational knowledge catch-up sessions
Pathway course catch-up sessions
Our commitment
The school is committed to ensuring the tuition fund is used in accordance with the Government’s guidance on the 16 to 19 tuition fund by:
publishing this guidance on the College website
